validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE + SPEC CHECK. The row's sole current ref (egyptoil-gas.com 'The Western Desert: Egypt's Giant Petroleum Reservoir', actually the raw EOG March-2020 magazine issue PDF) returns 200 but the automated verifier flagged 'value not found' for Status and never checked Length/Diameter/Owner beyond a raw 200 — a known content false-negative because the URL serves compressed PDF bytes that a naive fetch can't read as text. I pulled the PDF and ran it through pdftotext manually: it contains a 'Natural Gas Infrastructure in the Western Desert' pipeline table with a line-item exactly matching this row: 'Abu Sennan Spur | From: GPT | To: BED/Abu Sennan connector | Length: 45 km | Diameter: 14 in | Capacity: -' (dash = not reported, matching GEM's blank Capacity). Same article's prose independently states 'General Petroleum Company (GPC) established a plant for gas and condensate processing in Abu Sennan with a capacity of about 85 mmcf/d ... Hence the southern fields' production is linked to a distribution center on the Mediterranean Coast through Abu Sennan field' — corroborating Owner=General Petroleum Co and Fuel=Gas/PipelineType=transmission (this spur feeds the BED/AS-Ameryia trunk, GEM P3936, to the coast). So the existing ref is legitimate and DOES support Status(operating, inferred from being listed as existing infrastructure)/Fuel/PipelineType/Length/Diameter/Owner — the verifier FAIL is a screen artifact, not a real defect. Independent corroboration: GulfPub PE World Map (Dec-2025 scrape) lists TWO separate 'Abu Sennan Spur'-family lines both originating at 'GPT field' with diameter 14in exactly matching GEM/EOG on both: 'Abu Sennan Spur' GPT->Pipeline T junction 33km, and 'GPT - Abu Sennan Spur' GPT->Alam El Shawish 13km (33+13=46km, close to GEM/EOG's consolidated 45km). Web search of the geology literature (paper titles/abstracts, not independently fetchable — academia.edu/researchgate both 403 to bots — so not cited as refs) further confirms 'GPT' is a real, named oil/gas field within the Abu Sennan concession (distinct from the SWS and GPY blocks), consistent with the pipeline's stated origin. Existence: HIGH (2 independent sources — EOG trade-press table + GulfPub PE map — both name an Abu Sennan Spur-family line from GPT with matching diameter). Classification (transmission): consistent with GEM's treatment of the entire sibling 'spur' family (Obaiyed Spurline, Salam Spurline, Badr El Din Spur (1)/(2), Qasr-Shams, Shams-Obaiyed — all in the same source table, all classified transmission in GEM) — no reclassification warranted. No duplicate found against the 30-pipeline Egypt gas operating roster: P3937/P3938 'Badr El Din Spur' rows map 1:1 onto the table's 'Badr El Din Spur (1)/(2)' entries (dia 20/16, cap 180/150 — exact match), and none of the other 28 rows share GPT/Abu Sennan-specific endpoints, so P6689 is not a re-entry of another PID.

validity.recommendation: Note the length is well-supported at the consolidated (45km) granularity by the primary source, but GulfPub's independent, more granular breakdown (2 legs summing to 46km with different named termini) suggests the physical Abu Sennan Spur network may actually be two distinct legs rather than one continuous 45km line to a single 'BED/Abu Sennan connector'. Not an error requiring immediate correction, but flag for a future granularity review if/when GulfPub route geometry is examined for this cluster.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM Length=45km/Diameter=14in matches the EOG March-2020 table exactly (see above). GulfPub PE World Map (independent, Dec-2025 scrape) corroborates diameter (14.0in, exact match on both of its two candidate records) but splits the spur into 'Abu Sennan Spur' (GPT->Pipeline T junction, 33km, len DELTA 27% vs GEM's 45) and 'GPT - Abu Sennan Spur' (GPT->Alam El Shawish, 13km, len DELTA 71% vs GEM's 45). Neither single GulfPub record matches GEM's 45km alone, but the two sum to 46km — within 2% of GEM's figure — suggesting GEM/EOG's single 45km 'Abu Sennan Spur' may be a consolidated representation of what GulfPub resolves as two separate legs from the same GPT origin. This is a plausible, non-alarming explanation (aggregation vs. granular route-tracing) rather than an error, so I am not downgrading tier, but it should be on record given the material length delta against either individual GulfPub leg.

routes.corridor_desc: Per the EOG March-2020 industry table, this spur runs from 'GPT' (a named oil/gas field/facility inside the Abu Sennan concession — corroborated as a real field name by the geology literature, though those papers were bot-blocked and not citable) to a shared tie-in the same table calls the 'BED/Abu Sennan connector'. The Abu Sennan concession's bounding box (29 deg32'-29 deg49'N, 28 deg35'-28 deg59'E; ~260km west of Cairo, ~160km south of the Mediterranean coast) is sourced from nsenergybusiness.com; I used its centroid as the start point since GPT's exact sub-block position within the concession is not independently pinned down. The connector itself is not a mapped place in any source I could verify — it is also the terminus of the two ~130km 'Badr El Din Spur' lines (GEM P3937/P3938) from the Badr El Din/Sitra field cluster (BAPETCO lease, bounding box sourced from a Nature Scientific Reports paper on the Sitra field), and the origin of the ~160km 'BED/AS-Ameryia' trunk (GEM P3936) continuing north to the Ameriya gas complex near Alexandria. So the corridor is best understood as: Abu Sennan/GPT area -> WNW/NW across the Abu Gharadig Basin -> a gas-gathering hub in the general vicinity of the Badr El Din/Sitra fields -> (separately) onward to the coast. I am NOT plotting a specific connector coordinate since none is sourced — this is a loose area-to-area corridor bound, not a route.
routes.researcher_notes: No pipeline-specific GIS/route source found; endpoints are approximated only as field/concession-area centroids from verified sources, with the true connector site left unsourced (null lat/lon) rather than fabricated. This supports at most a 'low' RouteAccuracy suggestion — enough to bound a rough corridor for a human routes-repo pass, not enough to draw a defensible centerline.

summary: P6689 Abu Sennan Spur Gas Pipeline: existence/classification/owner CONFIRMED (high) via the row's own ref (verified by hand-decoding its PDF, contra the automated screen) plus independent GulfPub corroboration (diameter exact match); length carries a medium-tier caveat because GulfPub's more granular breakdown (2 legs, 33+13=46km) doesn't map 1:1 onto GEM's single 45km figure though the sum is close; EndLocation duplicating StartLocation ('Abu Sennan'->'Abu Sennan') is a genuine, fixable data error (true terminus per the source is 'BED/Abu Sennan connector'), flagged but not force-corrected. No duplicate against the 30-row roster. Route: only a loose, low-accuracy area-to-area corridor could be sourced (concession/field bounding-box centroids); the connector's exact site is unsourced and left null.
